summary: Save Search is a command, and what a Smart Folder searches with lasts as long as its search. src/actions.rs: `SaveSearch` in `actions!`, bound to `secondary-s` in the Finder context (after ToggleFilter in `key_table`), and `Save Search…` in the Edit menu after Find. src/finder/dialogs.rs: `save_search` is the handler (registered on the Finder root in mod.rs); during a search it opens `save_smart_folder_dialog` (now private), outside one it pushes a warning notification. The dialog's builder runs every frame and reads the typed name: a `smart-summary` line worded by the new `SmartFolder::summary()` (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs), a `smart-exists` note and a Replace label while a Smart Folder has that name, and the primary button disabled with no name. `submit_smart_folder` says Replaced when it replaced one. src/finder/bars.rs: the Save button (`save-smart-folder`, moved out of the filter bar, same ID) is in `render_scope_bar` after the spacer, before the funnel, with `tooltip_with_action`. src/finder/toolbar.rs: `Save Search…` in `actions_menu` above `Filter with Nushell…`, disabled outside a search. src/finder/filter.rs: `add_smart_folder` replaces in place. `Finder::smart_folder_setup: Option<SmartFolderSetup>` holds `before` and `opened` (private `SearchSetup`: kind, scope, contents, the filter as the bar's field has it, filter_open) and `missing` (the scope folder that couldn't be found). `open_smart_folder` ends the search, then calls `enter_smart_folder`, which records the window's own setup, assigns the Smart Folder's (the kind into `published` too, so it is never published) and puts the filter in through `replace_filter`. `leave_smart_folder` takes the setup and puts back each part that still equals `opened`; it is the first thing `end_search` does and is called from `on_search_event`'s Change when the field is empty. `shows_smart_folder(&SmartFolder)` is the sidebar's test for the marked row: the whole search equal to the saved one through `current_smart_folder`, with a scope folder that was missing when it was opened counted as its own. src/model.rs: `SavedSearch.smart: Option<(KindFilter, String)>`, set by `live_search` while a setup is in force and applied by `restore_search` through `enter_smart_folder`, so Back and Forward return to a Smart Folder's whole search and it ends like one again. src/finder/sidebar.rs: `smart_is_active` calls `shows_smart_folder`; `smart_is_active_for_test` for tests. docs/manual.md and README.md are updated; CHANGELOG.md is not, per the guide.
changelog: Smart Folders are easier to save, and opening one no longer changes how you search afterwards. **Save** is now in the scope bar of every search (it was in the Nushell filter bar), Cmd+S does the same, and **Save Search…** is in the Actions and Edit menus. The dialog says everything it saves: the words, Name or Contents, the folder or This Computer, the kind, and the filter. When a Smart Folder already has the name you type, the dialog says that saving replaces it, its button reads Replace, and the replaced one keeps its place in the sidebar. A Smart Folder's kind, scope, Name or Contents, and filter now last as long as its search. When you go elsewhere, press Escape, or empty the search field, the window searches the way it did before and its own filter is back. Before, a folder opened after a Smart Folder stayed filtered, and the Smart Folder's kind became the kind of new tabs and of the next launch. What you change by hand while a Smart Folder is open stays. If you used a Smart Folder to load a filter and then browsed folders with it, type that filter in the filter bar instead. Back and Forward return to a Smart Folder's search with its kind and filter. A Smart Folder's row is highlighted only while its whole search is showing, so two with the same words no longer light up together, and one whose folder is gone says that it is searching This Computer instead.
behaviour_changes: Saving. The scope bar of every search has a Save button (folder-cog icon, tooltip "Save this search as a Smart Folder" with its keys). The Nushell filter bar no longer has one. Seen in my own pictures in light and dark, and at 620 px where the bar wraps the Kind menu to a second line.

Cmd+S (Ctrl+S on Linux and Windows, and Ctrl+S as well with --term on a Mac) opens Save Smart Folder during a search, from the files, the search field, the filter field and the Nushell panel's field (probed each). Outside a search it shows a warning: "Search for something first, then save it as a Smart Folder". With a dialog open it does nothing (probed: no second dialog, no notification).

Actions menu: "Save Search…" above "Filter with Nushell…", disabled outside a search, with its key. Edit menu on the Mac's menu bar: "Save Search…" after Find; it is enabled whenever the window has the keyboard, and outside a search it gives the same warning as the key.

The dialog's line reads, for example, "Shows names matching “log” in “Studio”, kind Image, where size > 1kb. Kept up to date." It says "files containing" for Contents and "on This Computer" with no folder, leaves the kind out for Any Kind and for Contents, and says "filtered with | …" for a pipeline. It was "Shows “log” where size > 1kb, kept up to date."

While the typed name is one a Smart Folder has, a second line says "“x” is already a Smart Folder. Saving replaces it." and the button reads Replace. The name starts as the search's words, so the note is there from the start when a Smart Folder is called that. With no name the button is disabled, and Return still does nothing.
Replacing keeps the Smart Folder's row where it was (it used to move to the end), and the notification says "Replaced “x” in the sidebar".

A Smart Folder's kind, scope (Search Only in Folder), Name or Contents, filter, and the filter bar being open or closed end with its search: going anywhere, Cmd+Up, Show in Enclosing Folder (Cmd+Return, probed on the merged trunk), Escape in the files or the search field, the field's clear button, emptying the field, Back, New Folder, opening another Smart Folder. The window then has what it had before, including a filter of its own that the Smart Folder had displaced (probed with a real `nu`: the folder is back under the window's own filter with the same item selected). Before, the next folder stayed filtered and later searches kept the kind and scope.
Consequence: a Smart Folder can no longer be used to load a filter and then browse folders with it.

A part changed by hand while a Smart Folder is open (the Kind menu, the scope chips, Name/Contents, the filter typed or removed, the bar opened or closed) stays as changed. A part changed and then changed back to the Smart Folder's own goes back to the window's earlier one (equality decides). Escape in the Smart Folder's filter field empties it and leaves the bar open, as it does for any filter, so the empty bar is still open after the search ends (probed).
Other words typed during its search, a Search Syntax example clicked, or words sent with `fff gui` without a path keep its kind, scope, Name/Contents and filter until that search ends.
Its kind no longer reaches settings.json, new tabs or new windows, on opening or on leaving. A kind picked from the Kind menu while it is open is still a choice and is saved.
A filter typed less than 400 ms before a Smart Folder is clicked is no longer applied over the Smart Folder's filter, and is back, applied, when the Smart Folder's search ends.
When the filter bar goes away with the keyboard in its field (a Smart Folder's search ended by a key, or a filterless Smart Folder's search coming back by a key), the files get the keyboard.

Back and Forward return to a Smart Folder's search with its kind and filter as well as its words, scope and Name/Contents, and its row is marked again. All of that ends with the search again; for any other search, scope and Name/Contents still stay on, as before.

To the history, a Smart Folder's search and a hand-typed search with the same words, scope and Name/Contents are two different steps. Typing a search and then clicking a folder-scoped Smart Folder that is exactly that search leaves the typed one a step behind; before they counted once.

A Smart Folder's row is highlighted only while words, kind, place, Name/Contents and filter are all its own, so two with the same words and different kinds no longer light up together. A search typed by hand that is exactly a Smart Folder's lights its row, and so does the search right after it is saved.

A Smart Folder whose folder can't be found shows a warning each time it is opened: "<path> can’t be found, so “name” is searching This Computer". Its row is highlighted while that search shows (a review fix: the implementer's version left it unmarked), until the scope is changed by hand. After Back or Forward to such a search the row is not marked; see the notes.

Tree sidebar: with the arrow keys, a Smart Folder is where the keyboard is only while its whole search shows, so Up no longer skips from the last of several Smart Folders with the same words to the first one.
left_out: "Rename…" and "Update with Current Search" in a Smart Folder's right-click menu, and the hashing of names in `sidebar_key` that only a rename needs. The plan of record has them as optional (Part E). Saving under the same name updates a Smart Folder in place and says so. The menu still has only Remove from Sidebar.
CHANGELOG.md, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.

The exact handling of "changed by hand and changed back" (forgetting the remembered value inside set_kind, set_scope and set_search_contents), which the verifier gave as an option. Equality is used. For the kind this leaves one seam, probed: own kind Any, a Smart Folder for Folder, pick Document, pick Folder again, leave. The tab is back at Any, and the saved setting (what new tabs and the next launch start with) is Folder, the kind picked last.

No test pins the wording of the three notifications; the harness can only count them. Two tests count them and my pictures show two of the three texts (nothing to save, folder gone); the implementer's show all three.
No test covers the Edit menu's item; `set_menus` is tested for no item and Linux shows no menu bar. `SaveSearch` is in every_menu_bar_action_has_a_handler.

The folder that couldn't be found is not kept with the search in the history, so Back or Forward to such a Smart Folder's search runs it the same (This Computer, its kind and filter) with its row unmarked.
Nothing for regex-content-search, which is not on the trunk: there is no contents mode to save or restore yet.

`cargo clippy --features term` was not run. src/term calls nothing this change touched (grepped: no use of the Smart Folder functions, `SavedSearch`, `save_search` or the filter functions in src/term, src/macos.rs, src/win.rs, src/server, src/workspace.rs or src/lib.rs).

review_fixes: src/finder/filter.rs, src/finder/sidebar.rs: a Smart Folder whose folder can't be found is marked in the sidebar while the search it was opened as shows. The implementer followed the plan to the letter (whole-search equality, and This Computer is not the saved folder), so the row was never marked, with a test that said so. In list mode that is only a clicked row left unmarked. In the tree sidebar it was a trap: `tree_cursor` (src/finder/folder_tree.rs) takes the first marked line as where the arrow keys are, so after Up onto such a Smart Folder the next Up started again from the place below and opened the same Smart Folder again, with its warning, on every press. The trunk before this change marked the row (words and filter only), so Up went on. Probed on the implementer's commit and on 323f173. The fix: `SmartFolderSetup.missing` remembers the folder that couldn't be found (set in `open_smart_folder`), and the new `shows_smart_folder` counts This Computer as that folder for the one Smart Folder saved with it. A scope chosen by hand unmarks it, as for any other part.

Both fail without the fix (run).

notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the rebased tree, which is the trunk commit 60df179: 638 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures (624 on the trunk before it, plus the 14 tests above that are new). The implementer's commit was 30773a7 on 323f173. The trunk moved by three commits while I reviewed (c28f42d, 66d4fad, a6b81fc); the rebase had one conflict, in the manual's Actions list, resolved to keep both items. `git push . HEAD:search-ui-polish` fast-forwarded a6b81fc..60df179 and `git push origin search-ui-polish` went through; `git ls-remote origin` reads 60df179.

How it was checked. I read every changed function whole and followed the callers. Every path that ends a search goes through `end_search` (navigate, go_up, reveal_in_place and with it the new Show in Enclosing Folder, show_step, Escape in the files, New Folder, a Smart Folder for This Computer) or through the search field's change to nothing; `set_query` has no other caller that passes nothing. `enter_smart_folder` runs only after `end_search` in both callers, so `before` is always the window's own. `InputState::set_value` emits no Change (gpui-base input/base/state.rs), `clean` does. `leave_smart_folder` runs before the words go, against the plan's order: the search that `set_filter` starts there is replaced in the same update by `set_query("")` (new generation, task and abort flag), in both callers. I ran throwaway probes through the real window (deleted): the kind changed and changed back; Escape in the filter field; other words then away and Back; a This Computer Smart Folder from the Trash and from Recents; Cmd+S from each field and inside the dialog; a hand-made Smart Folder with no words; one Smart Folder opened from another, then four Backs and four Forwards with a filter and a kind of the window's own; `open_request` with and without a path; Cmd+F and type over; the clear button; a result opened and Back; Cmd+Up; New Folder; a new tab; saving over the Smart Folder that is open; a real `nu` with a filter of the window's own. And a walk of 700 random steps (four Smart Folders, one with a folder that is gone and one searching contents; going to folders, Back, Forward, Escape in the files and in the field, Cmd+Up, typed words, Back from the filter field), asserting after every step that with no search the setup is the window's own and the bar closed, that a marked Smart Folder's kind, Name or Contents and filter are the ones showing, that at most one is marked, that the saved kind stays Any, and every 25 steps that keys still reach the window. No step failed. My own pictures: the scope bar light, and dark at 620 px; the dialog with the Replace note; the Actions menu outside a search; the nothing-to-save notice; the tooltip; an open Smart Folder beside one with the same words; the folder back whole after Back; the folder-gone warning before and after the fix.

The three ways I thought it most likely to hurt someone, each checked against the code. (1) Something of a Smart Folder stays on, or the window's own filter or kind is lost: the list of search endings above, the walk, and the probes. (2) Back or Forward shows another list than was left, or loses or repeats a step: `SavedSearch` equality now includes `smart`; `past_repeats` still counts a Smart Folder opened twice once (tests/finder.rs passes) and a kind changed by hand in between makes two steps, which is right. (3) The keyboard goes dead or is trapped: the filter bar going away with the caret in it is handed to the files (tested); the tree sidebar's arrows were trapped by a folder that is gone (fixed, above); Cmd+S collides with no key of the kit or the app.

Known seams of this change, none of them new harm.
- The kind, changed and changed back (see left_out).
- Back or Forward to the search of a Smart Folder whose folder is gone: its row is unmarked. To mark it, keep the missing folder with the search (`SavedSearch.smart`) and hand it to `enter_smart_folder`.
- Text typed in a Smart Folder's filter field less than 400 ms before its search ends counts as typed by hand and is applied to the next folder.
- A Smart Folder with no words, which only a hand edit of settings.json makes, keeps its setup while the folder shows, until the next navigation or the next search's end.
- Move Tab to New Window carries a search's words only (it always did), so a Smart Folder's search arrives as a plain search for its words. Before this change the Smart Folder's kind went along through the saved setting.
- Not run on macOS or Windows. No cfg-gated code is touched. On a Mac check once: Cmd+S in a search and outside one, the Edit menu's item, and Ctrl+S with --term (some terminals keep it for flow control).

For the briefs still to come.
- focus-lost-recovery (lane-e): `Finder::replace_filter` (src/finder/filter.rs) gives the files the keyboard itself when the filter bar goes away with the caret in its field. That happens on a key, not on a click: Back from a Smart Folder's filter field, or Forward to a filterless Smart Folder's search from the window's own filter field. Your `on_focus_lost` net would catch the same; with it this hand-off is spare, and harmless, since it moves the keyboard before the field goes and no focus is lost. the_keyboard_stays_in_the_window_when_a_smart_folder_takes_the_filter_bar_away has to keep passing either way. A click on a Smart Folder's row in the list sidebar still leaves the keyboard with the browser as a whole (probed: files_focused is false afterwards); that is your second part, untouched here. In the tree sidebar the click focuses the tree first, as before.
- live-search-results (lane-d): a Smart Folder's search is an ordinary `run_search` with the window's kind, scope, Name or Contents and filter, which `enter_smart_folder` has set, so running it again needs nothing more. Do not run it again through `end_search`, `set_query("")` or anything else that ends the search: `end_search` now starts with `leave_smart_folder`, which gives the window its own setup back.
- regex-content-search: the orchestrator's note stands. For a Smart Folder to save and restore the mode: a field on `SmartFolder` (config.rs; `summary()` should word it, and its unit test lists every case), `current_smart_folder`, the private `SearchSetup` in filter.rs with `search_setup`, the assignment in `enter_smart_folder` and the put-back in `leave_smart_folder` (only if still as opened), and `SavedSearch` (beside `contents`, or in `smart` if only Smart Folders should bring it back). `shows_smart_folder` compares whole `SmartFolder`s, so the sidebar's mark follows by itself once `current_smart_folder` fills the field. `enter_smart_folder` has seven arguments with `self`; one more trips clippy's too_many_arguments, so bundle them. In the scope bar the Save button sits after the flex spacer, before the funnel.
- recent-searches: a search ends in two places, `end_search` and `on_search_event`'s Change with an empty field, and both call `leave_smart_folder` first, while the words are still set. Words put in through `set_query` while a Smart Folder's search shows run with its kind, scope and filter, as typed words do; if a recalled search should be a search of its own, call `end_search` first. Cmd+S is taken. The scope bar has one more control.
- restore-session-tabs: while a Smart Folder is open, a tab's `config.kind_filter`, `scope`, `search_contents` and filter are the Smart Folder's, not the tab's own (`published.kind_filter` mirrors the kind so that it isn't saved). If you save a tab's search state, save the window's own (it is `smart_folder_setup.before`, private to filter.rs; add an accessor) or the Smart Folder's whole search, not a mix. `SavedSearch` has a new field, `smart`.
- empty-state-messages: its problem (4) is half gone: a Smart Folder's kind no longer stays on after its search, and neither does its filter, so "No Items" in a folder no longer follows from a Smart Folder click. An Any Kind button in a Smart Folder's search calls `set_kind`, which is a choice: it is saved and stays after the search. The scope bar's Kind button is unchanged; Save was added before the funnel.
- collapsible-sidebar-sections: the mark of a Smart Folder's row is `shows_smart_folder` (filter.rs), and the tree's keyboard takes the first marked line as its place (`tree_cursor`). A collapsed Smart Folders section that hides the marked line would send the arrows on from another marked line; see the first item under Found, not fixed. tests/folder_tree.rs the_arrows_go_on_past_a_smart_folder_whose_folder_is_gone walks Up from ("loc", 0) through the Smart Folders, so the section has to be open there.
- context-menus-fit, split-view-toolbar-clip: `actions_menu` (src/finder/toolbar.rs) has a new row, Save Search…, above Filter with Nushell…, disabled outside a search; tests/controls.rs save_search_is_on_a_key_and_in_the_actions_menu clicks it by label. A Smart Folder's row menu still has only Remove from Sidebar.
- split-active-pane, type-select-space, go-to-folder-keyboard and anything else that adds to src/actions.rs: `SaveSearch` is in `actions!` after ToggleFilter and `secondary-s` is bound in the Finder context; both test lists in tests/controls.rs (every_command_a_tooltip_names_has_keys_to_show, every_menu_bar_action_has_a_handler) have it.
- search-start-no-flash: `open_smart_folder` and `restore_search` still end the search before `enter_smart_folder` and `set_query`, the order search-skeleton-flash asked to keep. Leaving a Smart Folder that has a filter rebuilds the result rows once more (in `set_filter`) just before `set_query("")` clears them.
- query-history-boost: nothing to do; a Smart Folder's search still passes its kind and scope to the engine as any search does.
- select-all-perf: `shows_smart_folder` builds one `SmartFolder` (four small clones) for each Smart Folder row on each sidebar frame while a search shows, and clones the name when none does. It doesn't grow with the folder.

Found, not fixed (there before, outside this brief).
- Tree sidebar, keyboard: Down cannot get past the first Smart Folder while a line above it is still marked. `tree_cursor` (src/finder/folder_tree.rs) takes the first line `line_is_active` marks as where the arrow keys are. A Smart Folder that searches This Computer doesn't change the place, so Recents, or the tree's selected folder under Favorites, stays marked above it, and every Down opens the same Smart Folder again. A folder-scoped one does the same when its folder's line is above the Smart Folders. Probed on 323f173 and on the final code with two Smart Folders for different words, from a favorite and from Recents: nine presses of Down never reach the second one, nor Locations below. Up from below works, since the Smart Folder's line then comes before the place's. A fix to try: in `tree_cursor`, let a marked `Line::Smart` win over the other marked lines, since the search is what shows. Since this change, two Smart Folders with the same words no longer both count, which was a second way to stick.
- Sidebar: the manual says Cmd+click or middle-click opens any row in a new tab; a Smart Folder's row has only a plain click (`smart_row` in src/finder/sidebar.rs). Found by the implementer, read by me.
- With a Nushell filter on, a search's first results can show cut down by a keep-set that wasn't made for them. `apply_filter_to` starts a new run when the rows change and goes on applying the last run's `filter_keep` until the new one answers, so results are first held against what the filter kept of the folder's rows (usually none of them), for as long as `nu` takes. For a Smart Folder the folder's run is the one `set_filter` starts just before the words are set (the same order on 323f173); it counts only if it answers before the search does, as with a slow contents search. Found by the implementer; traced by me by reading, on both commits; not probed, since the test executor runs a `nu` to its end in one step.
- `open_smart_folder` asks the disk whether the scope folder is there (`is_dir()`) on the window's thread at click time; a folder on a volume that hangs would hang the window. Found by the implementer.
- Move Tab to New Window (`Workspace::move_tab_to_new_window`) opens the new window with the tab's place and words only, so any search loses its scope and Name or Contents there, and a Smart Folder's search its kind and filter as well.
